title: Coder One: measure the controller's contribution with matched targeted tests
body:
## Goal

Find out whether Coder One's controller (Jev briefing, checks, support, repair, escalation) adds passes or saves cost when the executor settings are the same, on a targeted task set, before any further suite runs.

## Why

The 26-task comparison (11 vs 9 passes, 45% cheaper) changed effort, tools, system prompt, and cache lifetime along with the controller. The matched pilot held those fixed and found no measurable controller benefit on two tasks (6/6 plain vs 5/6 Coder). See https://github.com/OpenAgentsInc/openagents/blob/main/docs/terminal-bench/2026-09-23-what-we-have-learned.md, lesson 1.

## Work

1. Add a fair baseline arm: Claude Code on Opus 5.5 at medium effort with the same six tools, system prompt, and five-minute cache as Coder One.
2. Pick about 10 targeted tasks: the tasks other agents solve at least 80% of the time that we fail, plus a few we pass.
3. Run both arms, 3 attempts each, interleaved, using the fast loop from the iteration-time issue.
4. Report passes with intervals, cost, and time per arm and per task, and attribute differences to controller components using the invocation records.

## Acceptance

A table stating, with its uncertainty, whether the controller changes pass rate or cost on these tasks, published in docs/terminal-bench/. No full suite.
